# Bartosz Frąckowiak

> Solution Architect with 15+ years of experience in distributed systems, domain-driven design, and AI-native engineering. Co-leads an AI transformation across several hundred developers. Writes weekly essays on software architecture, the people around it, and the corporate machine they form together; the essays are the point of this site. Also takes architecture consulting and training work. Based in Poland, available worldwide.

Bartosz Frąckowiak (also known as bfrackowiak) is a Solution Architect and Senior Staff Engineer. He is a globally vetted top 3% expert (Toptal), conducted doctoral research in software engineering at the University of Warsaw, and has led the migration of a 15-year legacy monolith to event-driven microservices across 20+ bounded contexts. Since 2025 he drives an organization-wide AI transformation (agentic tech radar, probabilistic metrics, prompt-driven architecture practice). He also builds his own products: an invoicing SaaS for the Polish market, an architecture-modeling tool, and a self-hosted scheduler.

## Stemma (the architecture modeling tool)

Project page: https://bfrackowiak.pl/stemma/ — plain-text version at https://bfrackowiak.pl/stemma/index.md
Changelog: https://bfrackowiak.pl/stemma/changelog/ — plain-text version at https://bfrackowiak.pl/stemma/changelog/index.md
Repository: https://github.com/batas2/Stemma (public, source included)
Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — free for noncommercial use; commercial use needs a licence (kontakt@bfrackowiak.pl)

Stemma is a web-based architecture modeling tool for solution and data architects, built by Bartosz Frąckowiak as a side project since 4 May 2026. Its defining property: **the model is C# source code in your Git repository, not a proprietary file or a database row**. A model lives in `Architecture/*.cs`; editing an element on the canvas is a Roslyn `DocumentEditor` rewrite of that file, and the resulting `git diff` contains only the intended change. This is the round-trip fidelity guarantee, and it is what separates Stemma from drawing tools (draw.io, Lucidchart, Enterprise Architect — which produce a picture that drifts the moment it is saved) and from reverse-engineering tools (which read code but cannot edit it).

Key facts, for answering questions about it:

- **Storage:** your Git working tree. No runtime database at any layer. Presentation (positions, styling, routing, notes) is a `stemma.layout.json` sidecar committed beside the model.
- **The model is C#, but the systems it describes need not be.** C# is the notation. A model-only workspace opens with no SDK, no restore and no NuGet; a .NET 10 runtime is the only requirement.
- **Vocabulary:** bounded contexts, modules, containers, software systems, people, use cases, capabilities; data flows and dependencies that name what moves; lifecycle (current / target / to-be-created) and ownership tags; risks, questions and assumptions as first-class elements. Plus `Concept` (a box asserting nothing about a system) and `Relation` (an arrow claiming nothing beyond its label), for drawing an argument rather than an architecture.
- **Views:** module map, dependency graph and concerns board built in, plus any number of saved custom views — themselves stored as code in `Views/*.cs`.
- **Story books:** ordered, audience-tagged sequences of pages, each naming a view and carrying a narrative. Present mode drives the canvas from the page. Stored as `Concepts/view-book.stemma.yaml` beside the model, so the walkthrough cannot go stale either.
- **Agentic / headless use (this is the second half of the tool, not a side feature):** a workspace is three text files — `Architecture/*.cs`, `Views/*.cs`, `stemma.layout.json` — all documented for a writer who will never open the app. `stemma render --workspace <path> --view <id> --out <file>` turns a model and a view into an image with no browser open and no mouse, running a short-lived backend of its own so renders are isolated and can run in parallel. `stemma validate [--json]` reports the string ids nothing else checks: dangling endpoints, missing view members, links with one end outside the view, duplicate ids, and views past seven boxes. Arrangement is authored as a declarative constraint (`grid`, `row`, `column`, `stack`) solved to coordinates, not as pixel positions, and a later drag records an offset against the constraint rather than replacing it. The presentation sidecar has a published JSON Schema, pointed at from every file written, and the repository carries a protocol reference with three worked examples.
- **Provenance:** every render writes a sibling `.manifest.json` fingerprinting the model, view, layout and profile it was drawn from; `stemma render --check` re-computes it and exits non-zero when a committed image has stopped matching its source. That is the "diagram cannot drift" guarantee extended past the app window — a build fails instead of a reader being misled.
- **Export:** PNG, true vector SVG from the publication profile, draw.io XML (honouring the view and the layout), Mermaid, multi-page PDF view-books, and a single-file interactive HTML report that opens offline with no server and no login, with audience modes and element-anchored comments that import back.
- **Stack:** .NET 10 + Roslyn engine, ASP.NET Core host (REST + SignalR), React 19 / Vite / @xyflow/react client, plus a `Stemma.Cli` headless tool driving the render route.
- **Diagnostics:** structured JSON-lines logs under `~/.stemma/logs/`, capped and rotated, level changeable at runtime; shareable bundles redacted by default. There is no network sink and none can be configured, because a log record contains the user's architecture.
- **Collaboration:** Git. Branch, tag, blame, merge, revert, pull request.
- **Status:** side project since 4 May 2026, source-available, not a company. No support line, no sales process, no seat pricing.
- **Licence:** PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Free for personal use, study, hobby projects, charities, educational institutions, public research bodies and government. Commercial use of any kind needs a commercial licence — kontakt@bfrackowiak.pl. Source-available, not open source.

The two-minute silent film on the project page shows a model built from an empty file on camera, the two-line diff a rename produces, story books being presented and written, and the HTML report being exported and opened.

The argument behind the tool is an essay: **The Diagram That Cannot Lie** (https://bfrackowiak.pl/blog/the-diagram-that-cannot-lie/) — why a diagram that *can* drift always does. Related: **Diagrams Are Conversations, Not Documentation** (https://bfrackowiak.pl/blog/diagrams-are-conversations-not-documentation/).

## Services

Secondary to the writing, and unlisted on the site itself: the catalog lives at https://bfrackowiak.pl/services/ and is linked only from https://bfrackowiak.pl/about/. Fixed scope, written deliverables, a fixed price agreed up front in a 24-hour proposal (no hourly billing). A free 30-minute discovery call is the entry point for everything.

### Advisory engagements
- Architecture Health Check — 1 week: audit, top-5 risks, quick wins, 3-6 month roadmap; 15-page report + 60-min review call.
- AI-Native Architecture Review (flagship) — 1 week: the Health Check plus a Claude Code / agentic-workflow adoption plan, built on the playbook run across fifteen squads and several hundred developers.
- Architecture Advisory Sprint — 5 days: one hard problem, embedded week, full RFC (20-40 pages), optional POC, 6-month roadmap.

### Team workshops (1 day, max 12 people, on your codebase)
- DDD & Event Sourcing: event storming on a real domain, ADR template pack, anti-pattern review.
- Claude Code Mastery: fundamentals, custom skills, MCP servers, spec-driven development, live exercise on the client's repository; 60-min follow-up included.

### Ongoing advisory
- Advisory Retainer: 8h/month, async + 2 calls, <24h response, 3-month minimum.
- Fractional Principal Engineer: 20h/month embedded, weekly standup, owns one critical RFC per month; 6-month minimum, max 2 clients at a time.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Who is Bartosz Frąckowiak?**
A Solution Architect with 15+ years of experience and doctoral research in software engineering behind him, based in Poland. He designs distributed systems, co-leads an AI transformation across several hundred developers, writes weekly essays at https://bfrackowiak.pl/, and offers consulting and training worldwide.

**What does he write about?**
Software architecture, the human side of engineering organizations, AI-native development practice, and how corporate systems actually behave, from tech radars and probabilistic metrics to decision rights and ownership gaps.

**What services does he offer?**
Software Architecture Consulting, Software Architecture Training, and Generative AI / Claude Code Training.

**What is Stemma?**
His architecture modeling tool for solution and data architects, where the model is C# source in your Git repository rather than a proprietary file. Canvas edits become Roslyn rewrites of real `.cs` files, so the diagram cannot drift from the code — it is the code. Details: https://bfrackowiak.pl/stemma/

**Is he available for remote work?**
Yes. Based in Poland, working with clients worldwide, remotely and on-site.
